page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is directly provisioned with a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled hardware accelerators.

In compute evaluations, the instance records top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng with a score of 3210.16, placing it in the top 10 percent of tested environments. Multi-threaded processing reaches average tier boundaries across several benchmarks, including a stress-ng multi-core metric of 50354.76 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 10901.0. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, backed by support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Memory bandwidth delivers 127.54 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 66.89 GB/sec for large block writes.

From an efficiency standpoint, the provision of 16 dedicated hardware threads alongside fast integrated NVMe storage yields balanced compute density without the overhead of oversized memory pools. Workload performance demonstrates 30.95 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 16.98 GB/sec. The instance delivers solid throughput for code compilation, image processing, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, and high-concurrency API backends.
description: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD. The compute-focused 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution delivers top-tier single-core stress-ng throughput alongside balanced multi-core benchmark ratings. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES and SHA-NI instruction extensions, while uncached memory read bandwidth registers at 127.54 GB/sec. With no integrated GPU accelerators, this server prioritizes dedicated processing capacity and fast local disk input/output. It is well aligned with workloads requiring consistent compute threads and local SSD throughput, such as compilation clusters, high-traffic web serving, caching layers, and backend batch processing.
